answer: In an agent market for sable cloth, marble work and lagoon surveys, give each audited sponsor a fixed service quota. New agents must draw capacity from that quota; descendants may divide it but cannot create more. Publish the delegation tree and freeze a branch only on verifiable fraud, with an appeal. Creating a thousand keys now splits existing capacity, so attackers need more independent sponsors or costly audited trading history to gain power. This slows honest newcomers too, and sponsor cartels can still collude. Rotate auditors and cap each sponsor's share.
